Article Title: Another Punjab MP faces SIR trouble; ECI clarifies Dharamvira Gandhi’s name ‘very much there’
Article Text:
ECI rejects Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday rejected Congress leader and Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim that his name and those of his family members were missing from Punjab's draft electoral roll published on August 13.According to an ECI statement, the Lok Sabha member and four of his family members are listed as electors in the Patiala Assembly constituency."Dr Dharamvira Gandhi, Member of Parliament, as well as his family members, wife Jagdamba Kaushal, daughter Rohani Prashar, daughter-in-law Chahat Sahuja, and son Nabendhu, are very much a part of the Draft Electoral Roll published on 13th August 2026. They are registered as electors in AC No 115 – Patiala, Part No 98, at Serial numbers 44 to 48," the poll panel said.The ECI’s clarification came a day after Dharamvira Gandhi, who was earlier associated with Punjab’s ruling AAP, claimed that his name and those of his family members were missing from the draft electoral roll published as part of the ECI’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in the state, where Assembly elections are due in February 2027.His claim came on the same day that BJP leader Raghav Chadha, another Punjab MP and another former AAP member, was marked as “shifted” in the state’s draft electoral roll. Chadha, who joined the BJP in April, accused his former party of "political vendetta." AAP rejected the allegation, pointing out that the SIR exercise is conducted by the Election Commission and not by a state government.Earlier, former diplomat Navdeep Suri had also alleged that he faced "difficulties" in “establishing my citizenship” during the Punjab SIR.
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday rejected Congress leader and Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim that his name and those of his family members were missing from Punjab's draft electoral roll. According to an ECI statement, the Lok Sabha member and four of hisFamily members are listed as electors in the PatialA Assembly constituency.

Article Title: ‘Taken to room, beaten’: YouTubers allege assault at Saket police station, cops deny
Article Text:
Two women YouTubers allege police personnel beat them at Saket police station.





NEW DELHI: Two women YouTubers alleged that they were assaulted by Delhi Police personnel after being taken to Saket police station on Thursday, while the police denied the charges, calling them “factually incorrect” and “misleading”.The women alleged that they were detained while covering an event in south Delhi and later assaulted inside the police station. A lawyer representing them has also filed a complaint over the alleged assault.According to the women, they had gone to cover the inauguration of a new wing at Max Hospital in Saket, attended by Union home minister Amit Shah and Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta. One of them alleged in a video circulated on social media that they intended to question the chief minister when they were detained and taken to Saket police station.She alleged that the two were taken to a room inside the police station and assaulted by police personnel. The women also claimed they were asked about their community and subjected to further assault and abuse. They alleged that both sustained injuries during the incident.Videos showing the two women displaying injury marks on different parts of their bodies were widely circulated on social media. The allegations, however, could not be independently verified.Delhi Police rejected the accusations and said the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.A senior police officer said they were not carrying identity cards and were repeatedly asked to move their vehicle after being informed about security arrangements for the VIP route.Police alleged that the women created a ruckus and manhandled a pregnant police officer. They were subsequently taken to Saket police station for further enquiry, police said.According to the police, the two women were free to leave within five to 10 minutes of reaching the police station and were not restrained. “Nobody was holding their hands or preventing them from leaving, but they chose not to go,” an officer said.Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal said claims that the women were assaulted for attempting to question the chief minister were “totally false, misleading and baseless”. He urged citizens and social media users not to circulate unverified information.Meanwhile, several journalists' organisations condemned the alleged assault and demanded a free and fair investigation.The Press Club of India, Indian Women’s Press Corps, Delhi Union of Journalists, Press Association and Kerala Union of Working Journalists, in a joint statement, alleged that the two freelance journalists were first manhandled near the venue before being taken to Saket police station.The organisations further alleged that police personnel assaulted the women inside the police station and called for punitive action against those responsible, including the station house officer. They also urged Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar to order a fair probe and appealed to the Press Council of India to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.The Aam Aadmi Party also attacked the BJP-led Delhi government over the allegations, with party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj claiming that the journalists were assaulted for asking questions of the chief minister.Delhi Police has maintained that the allegations are baseless and that the women were taken to the police station only after they allegedly refused to comply with security instructions on the designated VVIP route.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Two women YouTubers allege police personnel beat them at Saket police station. The women alleged they were detained while covering an event in south Delhi. Delhi Police rejected the accusations and said the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.

Article Title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay

NEW DELHI: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday after Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly.This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the state cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Speaking at an event in Kanyakumari on Saturday, Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would become the Prime Minister in 2029.The remarks came amid statements by TVK leaders projecting party chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post. TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan questioned why the Congress continued to be part of the TVK government despite the differences over the prime ministerial candidate."Repeated assertions by multiple TVK Ministers even inside on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly touting their leader as a probable Prime Minister is an outright rejection of the failed and dismal leadership of Rahul Gandhi by the TVK.Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the cabinet of the TVK government? Because the TVK minister's statements are a scathing vote of no confidence, and TVK is an alliance partner, but the Congress party still continues to be in the TVK government.Why is the Congress party not withdrawing support to the TVK government after their leader Rahul Gandhi has been insulted?" news agency ANI quoted Kesavan saying.The issue has gained further attention after a private media survey placed Vijay among the preferred candidates for PM in 2029, behind PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi.The TVK government was formed after the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, when the party emerged as the largest force and formed the government with support from VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI and CPI(M).
Article Summary: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday. Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly. This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.

Article Title: ​Govt delegation delays its visit to meet Jarange
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The govt delegation led by cabinet sub-committee chairperson and BJP minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil on Tuesday delayed its visit to Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district to meet quota activist Manoj Jarange.Despite the planned visit the delegation stayed back at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar till Tuesday night. Vikhe Patil said an administrative review is being taken first before meeting Jarange. “The talks with (Jarange) are not fixed yet. We have sent him information about different demands he raised and are expecting a response from his side first,” he told reporters.Jarange, whose agitation entered the fourth day on Tuesday, refused to undergo periodic medical check-up. Jalna district collector Ashmita Mittal visited the agitation site. “We held discussion with the core committee of Maratha reservation and apprised them about our side. We held dialogue with Jarange and also inquired about his health,” she said.Jarange has been demanding immediate issuance of Kunbi certificates to all eligible Marathas. He has also appealed to the Maratha community to adopt a “guerrilla strategy” and start reaching Mumbai quietly by Sept 12. If demands are not met by then, Jarange is expected to announce the final date for his march to Mumbai.
Article Summary: Jarange has been demanding immediate issuance of Kunbi certificates to all eligible Marathas. He has also appealed to the Maratha community to adopt a ‘guerrilla strategy’ and start reaching Mumbai quietly by Sept 12. If demands are not met by then, Jarange is expected to announce the final date for his march to Mumbai.

Article Title: Fadnavis is required where he is right now: Pankaja over his likely induction into PM Modi cabinet
Article Text:
Pankaja Munde

Kolhapur:





State environment minister and BJP member Pankaja Munde on Thursday said chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was required in the state amid opposition claims that he was soon to be inducted into the Narendra Modi-led Union Cabinet.“Such a decision cannot happen without the approval of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) or PM Modi. Fadnavis is an impactful and academically strong leader. I have worked with him for the last two-and-a-half decades. I can only pray that he grows beyond the position he currently holds. He is, however, needed where he is today,” Munde said, while speaking to reporters at Kolhapur Airport during her day-long visit.Her remarks came in response to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut ’s recent claim that PM Modi was keen to induct Fadnavis into the Union Cabinet.Munde also spoke on Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange’s ongoing hunger strike, saying state govt was making efforts to address his demands within the constitutional framework.Jarange is demanding caste certificates for Marathas whose Kunbi records have been traced, as well as implementation of provisions from the Kolhapur, Satara and Mumbai Gazetteers to recognise Marathas as Kunbis. “Govt has constituted a panel of ministers led by Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil to hold discussions with Jarange. Govt is trying to ensure justice to his demands within the framework of Constitution,” Munde said.Later in the day, she chaired a review meeting with officials of various govt agencies to discuss measures to tackle pollution in the Panchganga river.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis is an impactful and academically strong leader, says Pankaja Munde. Munde also spoke on Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange’s ongoing hunger strike, saying state govt was making efforts to address his demands within the constitutional framework.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: 2 women rescued from prostitution at Panvel lodge; manager, waiter pimp arrested
Article Text:
Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued two women from a prostitution racket (Photo credit: X)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued two women from a prostitution racket being operated at a lodge in Panvel area on Monday.The police arrested three accused including the lodge manager, a waiter and a pimp for providing the women to customers for sexual favour.The prostitution racket was busted by sending a decoy customer to the lodge from whom the accused accepted Rs 5,000 after selecting a woman who was provided at the lodge for indulging in sexual act.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of AHTU informed that, the arrested accused are Prakash Gupta, 28, the manager of Hotel Krantiveer Lodging and Boarding in Shirdhon village, Panvel taluka, a waiter Priyaranjan Rai, 18, and a middleman (pimp) Asgar Fakir Shaikh, 38, a resident of Vichumbe village, Panvel taluka.Shaikh had brought the women to the lodge for prostitution.The rescued women aged 30 year and 22 years hail from West Bengal and Assam respectively and resided in Panvel area.After registering an FIR at Panvel city police station on Tuesday, as per the Panvel court order, the two rescued women were sent to a women welfare centre in Mumbai.While, the three arrested accused were remanded to police custody till Aug 7.Inspector Ghadge said, "From the arrested accused we have seized their mobiles as evidence of text messages and photos of rescued women shared by the pimp share with the manager Gupta and waiter Rai for bringing the two women to the lodge to provide them to the decoy customer.Even pimp Shaikh's scooty was seized as it was used in the crime.""When questioned by the women cops, the rescued women claimed that Shaikh used to give them Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for having sex with each customer at the lodge. When inquired with the accused, it was learnt that the share of waiter Rai was ₹200 and the manager used to keep ₹800 for himself after booking a room at the lodge for the customer for having sexual acts with women, by neither entering the customer's name in the lodge register nor taking Aadhaar card copies," Ghadge said.
Article Summary: The police arrested three accused including the lodge manager, a waiter and a pimp. The prostitution racket was busted by sending a decoy customer to the lodge from whom the accused accepted Rs 5,000. The rescued women aged 30 year and 22 years hail from West Bengal and Assam respectively.

Article Title: Pune social media influencer held for sexual harassment, defamation against minister
Article Text:
Pune police arrested social media influencer Santosh Pandit on Thursday





PUNE: Police on Thursday arrested city-based social media influencer Santosh Pandit on charges of sexual harassment and defamation for allegedly posting videos containing obscene and abusive remarks against a Maharashtra minister and a PMC corporator.Opposition netas criticised the action, accusing govt of using police machinery to target a voice raising public issues. Police, however, maintained that the arrest was based on complaints and the content posted online.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar said people should avoid making objectionable statements and posting such videos on social media. “We will take stringent action against such people. On Thursday, we took one influencer into custody,” Kumar said.The police action came in the wake of a woman’s complaint. The woman in her complaint claimed that she had noticed two videos posted by Pandit on a popular online video-sharing website on Wednesday. “In the videos, Pandit was seen using lewd and abusive language against the minister and the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) corporator,” a Kothrud police officer said.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone III) Sagar Kawade told TOI that Pandit had been charged under sections 75 (sexual harassment), 356 (defamation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act.A local court sent Pandit to police custody till Sept 8.This was the second case registered against the influencer since Sunday. The Deccan Gymkhana police had registered a defamation case against him for allegedly using abusive language against the minister.Opposition accused state govt of misusing the police against the activists. State Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal said, “We do not support the use of foul language. However, Santosh Pandit is known for questioning authorities over civic issues. Our party protested Pandit’s late-night arrest.”Former minister and Congress senior Yashomati Thakur accused state govt of taking action against Pandit after he questioned senior BJP members Chandrakant Patil and Gopichand Padalkar. “The assault on anti-noise campaigner Vidyanand Bapat and arrest of Pandit shows that common man’s voice is being suppressed by govt. Common people can criticise politicians in a democratic society, but BJP can not take criticism. ”Bapat was on Thursday assaulted in the city allegedly by a member of a city-based Ganesh mandal amid the debate over use of high-decibel sound systems and DJs during Ganeshotsav.
Article Summary: Pune police arrested city-based social media influencer Santosh Pandit on charges of sexual harassment and defamation. Pandit allegedly posted videos containing obscene and abusive remarks against a Maharashtra minister and a PMC corporator. Opposition netas criticised the action, accusing govt of using police machinery to target a voice raising public issues.

Article Title: Tribal woman dies after family planning surgery in Salem; relatives lay siege to collectorate in protest
Article Text:
Over 100 relatives and villagers laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest

Salem:





A tribal woman died at the Attur govt Hospital on Thursday, after her health deteriorated following a sterilisation surgery at Pethanaickenpalayam primary health centre in Salem district.The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment. She had delivered her third child about 45 days ago.Over 100 relatives and villagers including her husband Matheawaran, 30, laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest. They alleged that a botched surgery had caused her death and demanded justice.Police held talks with the protesters and officials assured them that a proper inquiry would be held against the doctors concerned and appropriate action taken. The protesters subsequently withdrew their protest.Attur rural police have registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment.

Article Title: Duo assault Malaysian tourists near Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: A Malaysian man and his son were assaulted with deadly weapons by two unidentified men following a heated altercation near a petrol outlet at Navakkarai in Coimbatore district on Wednesday evening.The injured have been identified as Loganathan, 52, and his son Ugendran,21. Both were admitted to a private hospital in Madukkarai.According to police, 11 Malaysian tourists were travelling in a hired van from Alappuzha in Kerala to Chennai. Around 5.30pm, when the vehicle stopped near a petrol pump on the Cochin–Salem Bypass, an altercation broke out between the tourists and two men on the road. The argument quickly escalated, and the duo attacked Loganathan and Ugendran with sickles, damaging the vehicle’s windowpanes.Following the assault, the driver sped towards Madukkarai. However, the assailants chased the van on a two-wheeler. Upon reaching Madukkarai market, one of the pursuers brandished an object resembling a firearm, forcing the driver to stop the vehicle. As locals rushed to the scene upon hearing the commotion, the assailants fled.Alerted by locals, the Madukkarai police and senior officers arrived at the scene. They secured CCTV footage on the bypass to identify the culprits and establish the sequence of events.Police registered a case and launched a manhunt.
Article Summary: A Malaysian man and his son were assaulted with deadly weapons by two unidentified men following a heated altercation near a petrol outlet at Navakkarai in Coimbatore district on Wednesday evening. The duo attacked Loganathan and Ugendran with sickles, damaging the vehicle’s windowpanes.

Article Title: 9 boys held for sexually torturing classmate
Article Text:
Nine class VIII students have been arrested for allegedly sexually torturing their classmate inside a library at Government Higher Secondary School at Tharuvaikulam in Thoothukudi.





Thoothukudi: Nine class VIII students have been arrested for allegedly sexually torturing their classmate inside a library at Government Higher Secondary School at Tharuvaikulam in Thoothukudi.Police said though the boys, aged 13, were friends, the victim was often bullied by the others. Around 3.30pm on Aug 18, they were in the school library when the nine boys removed the victim’s trousers, hurt him, and applied chilli powder to his private parts. Upon the arrival of a teacher, the boys fled. A teacher informed the boy’s parents about the incident.On a complaint lodged by the his parents on Aug 31 at Vilathikulam All Women Police station, a case was registered under section 324 (mischief causing property damage), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 351(3) (criminal intimidation) of BNS and relevant sections of Pocso Act Police commenced investigation, and arrested five of the students on Sept 1, and the others subsequently. All nine were produced before the juvenile justice board, and lodged in a borstal home in Tirunelveli.
Article Summary: Police said though the boys, aged 13, were friends, the victim was often bullied by the others. Around 3.30pm on Aug 18, they were in the school library when the nine boys removed the victim's trousers, hurt him, and applied chilli powder to his private parts.

Article Title: Pay aid dues to victim of HIV blood transfusion: HC
Article Text:
Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman who was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018.





Madurai: Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman who was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018.A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel passed the order while hearing a batch of petitions seeking a direction to the state to provide compensation to the woman.Earlier, the court had directed the state to pay Rs25 lakh compensation and provide her govt employment. It was also directed to provide monthly financial assistance of Rs7,500 to the woman. The court further directed the state to construct a house and provide a two-wheeler to her. The hearing in the batch of petitions was adjourned to Sept 17.
Article Summary: Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman. The woman was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018. The court also directed to provide monthly financial assistance of Rs7,500 to the woman.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.

Article Title: Symbolic funeral of VC: Kerala HC relief for 17 Sanskrit varsity students
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has directed that the 17 students of Kalady Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit who had allegedly conducted a symbolic funeral of the vice-chancellor and also restrained her, be not arrested till Sept 11.A bench of Justice Kauser Edappagath issued the interim order in response to a pre-arrest bail petition filed by the students, including Archana P S of Palakkad, Abhijith K V of Ernakulam, and Rithisha of Kottayam. The bench further sought instructions from the state on the bail application and adjourned the case to Sept 11.According to the prosecution, on Aug 13, the petitioners and others, all SFI activists, unlawfully assembled on the campus and staged a symbolic funeral procession for the varsity vice-chancellor Ciza Thomas. It was further alleged that thereafter, the petitioners and other identifiable persons wrongfully restrained and confined Thomas, her staff members and syndicate members while they were leaving after attending a syndicate meeting. They allegedly pushed, assaulted and caused hurt to them. Later, the police registered a case based on a complaint filed by Thomas against the petitioners, prompting them to approach the HC seeking pre-arrest bail.
Article Summary: The high court has directed that the 17 students of Kalady Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit be not arrested till Sept 11. A bench of Justice Kauser Edappagath issued the interim order in response to a pre-arrest bail petition filed by the students.

Article Title: Kerala HC stays orders in Cashew Corp graft case
Article Text:
R Chandrasekharan

Kochi

:





A division bench of the Kerala high court has stayed the interim orders passed by a single bench, following which the state govt granted prosecution sanction under the PC Act against the accused persons in the Cashew Corporation graft case.A bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John issued the order in appeals filed by R Chandrasekharan, the first accused in the case and the former chairman of the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation (KSCDC), along with the second accused, K A Ratheesh, the former managing director. The orders stayed by the division bench include those by which the single bench quashed two govt orders denying prosecution sanction in the case and later upheld the govt order granting prosecution sanction and directed the CBI to proceed with the prosecution. In effect, the division bench’s order prevents the CBI from proceeding with the prosecution on the basis of the sanction pending disposal of the appeals.Chandrasekharan and Ratheesh challenged the single bench orders, contending that the bench had repeatedly quashed the govt orders that denied prosecution sanction against them in the case, thereby inducing the sanctioning authority to issue an order in favour of the CBI.They further claimed that the single bench had foreclosed their right to challenge the validity of the sanction order issued under Section 19(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, granting sanction to prosecute them. The appellants challenged the single bench’s exercise of judicial review of these govt orders in the contempt petition, contending that the court had exceeded its jurisdiction.The case arose from a petition filed by Kadakampally Manoj of Kollam seeking a CBI probe into the alleged large-scale corruption in the import and purchase of cashews by the KSCDC. Pursuant to the HC’s direction, the CBI conducted an investigation and arraigned Chandrasekharan and Ratheesh, along with two others, as accused. It subsequently sought prosecution sanction from the state govt, but the govt declined three times despite the court’s directions, prompting Manoj to file the contempt petition. While the court had initiated contempt proceedings, the state govt granted prosecution sanction in the case, which led to the present appeals.
Article Summary: A division bench of the Kerala high court has stayed the interim orders passed by a single bench. The state govt granted prosecution sanction under the PC Act against the accused persons in the Cashew Corporation graft case. In effect, the division bench’s order prevents the CBI from proceeding with the prosecution on the basis of the sanction pending disposal of the appeals.
